wikipedia.sentence:
We need to see if pronoun "यह" refers to an entity named elsewhere in same sentence. Sentence: "यह जलप्लावन एक 600 फीट लंबी और 180 फुट चौड़ी नहर थी।"

We have "यह जलप्लावन" - the pronoun "यह" is used before "जलप्लावन". The entity "जलप्लावन" is a noun, not a proper name. The pronoun refers to "जलप्लावन". The question: "entity that pronoun refers to is named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." Here the pronoun "यह" refers to "जलप्लावन". Is "जलप्लावन" a name? It's a noun, but it's the entity. The rule: if pronoun refers to something that is named elsewhere in same sentence, replace pronoun with that name. Here "जलप्लावन" appears right after pronoun, but is that considered "named elsewhere"? The pronoun "यह" modifies "जलप्लावन". The entity is "जलप्लावन". The pronoun refers to "जलप्लावन". The name appears in same phrase. So we can replace "यह" with "जलप्लावन". The sentence would become: "जलप्लावन जलप्लावन एक 600 फीट लंबी और 180 फुट चौड़ी नहर थी।" That seems redundant. But the instruction: replace pronoun with actual entity name, keeping everything else exactly as is. So we replace "यह" with "जलप्लावन". That yields "जलप्लावन जलप्लावन एक 600 फीट लंबी और 180 फुट चौड़ी नहर थी।" That seems odd but matches rule.

But maybe they consider "जलप्लावन" as the entity name, and pronoun "यह" refers to it

The rule: "entity that pronoun refers to is named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." Here the entity is "अभयारण्य". It is present as part of the phrase "यह अभयारण्य". But is that considered "named elsewhere"? The pronoun "यह" is a demonstrative, not a proper name. The entity is "अभयारण्य" which is a common noun, not a proper name. The instruction: "named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." In examples, they replace pronoun with the entity name. Example: "पूरा शहर ... और यह 111 फुट..." replaced "यह" with "शहर". They used the noun "शहर" which appears earlier. So they used the noun that appears earlier. Here "यह अभयारण्य". The noun "अभयारण्य" appears right after pronoun. So we can replace "यह" with "अभयारण्य". The resulting sentence: "अभयारण्य अभयारण्य घने वन के लिए जाना जाता है, जिसमें 30 मीटर तक के वृक्ष हैं।" That sounds odd: duplication. wikipedia.sentence:
We need to see if pronoun refers to an entity named elsewhere in same sentence. Sentence: "इनमें जो औसतन न्यून मात्रा के कण हैं, वे ही मिट्टी को उर्वरा बनाने के लिये आवश्यक हैं।"

Pronoun: "वे" refers to "जो औसतन न्यून मात्रा के कण हैं" i.e., the particles. The entity is described within same clause, not a separate name. The rule: entity must be named somewhere else in same sentence. Here "वे" refers to "जो ... कण". That's a description, not a proper name. But is that considered "named"? The entity is "कण". The phrase "जो औसतन न्यून मात्रा के कण हैं" is a noun phrase. The pronoun "वे" refers to that noun phrase. The instruction: "entity that pronoun refers to is named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." The noun phrase is present, but is it a name? It is a description, but still an entity mention. In examples, they replaced "यह" with "शहर" because "शहर" appears earlier. So they used the noun. Here "वे" refers to "कण". The noun "कण" appears in the clause. So we can replace "वे" with "कण". But need to keep everything else exactly as is. The original: "इनमें जो औसतन न्यून मात्रा के कण हैं, वे ही मिट्टी को उर्वरा बनाने के लिये आवश्यक हैं।"

Replace "वे" with "कण". But need to adjust grammar? The original: "वे ही ... आवश्यक हैं।" If we replace with "कण ही ... आवश्यक हैं।" That seems fine. So output: "इनमें जो औसतन न्यून मात्रा के कण हैं, कण ही मिट्टी को उर्वरा बनाने के लिये आवश्यक हैं।"
